title: New US Jet Breaks Sound Barrier in First Flight Test
speaker: VOA Learning English

sentences.en: An experimental aircraft developed by a private American company broke the sound barrier during a recent flight test.
sentences.zh: 美国一家私营公司研制的一架实验飞机在最近的一次飞行试验中打破了音障。

sentences.en: California-based company Boom Supersonic built the plane, named XB-1.
sentences.zh: 以加州为基地的Bom Supersonic公司 建造了这架飞机 名为XB -1

sentences.en: The company said the aircraft reached a speed of Mach 1.05 during a test on January 28.
sentences.zh: 该公司说,该飞机在1月28日的一次试验中达到1.05马赫的速度。

sentences.en: The test flight operated from the Mojave Air & Space Port in Mojave, California.
sentences.zh: 试飞从加利福尼亚莫哈韦的莫哈韦航空和空间港进行。

sentences.en: Any speed greater than Mach 1.0 breaks the sound barrier and is considered supersonic.
sentences.zh: 超过马赫1.0的任何速度都会打破音障,被视为超音速。

sentences.en: The American space agency NASA explains that at sea level, the speed of sound is estimated to be about 1,236 kilometers per hour.
sentences.zh: 美国航天局解释说,在海平面上,声音的速度估计约为每小时1,236公里。

sentences.en: In a statement, Boom Supersonic said the XB-1 demonstrator aircraft climbed to more than 35,000 feet before reaching Mach 1.0.
sentences.zh: Boom Supersonic说,XB-1型示威者飞机攀升到35 000多英尺,然后到达马赫1.0。

sentences.en: It recorded the speed within 11 minutes of taking off.
sentences.zh: 它记录了起飞11分钟内的速度。

sentences.en: The company also released a video feed of the supersonic test flight.
sentences.zh: 该公司还播放了超音速测试飞行的录像。

sentences.en: The company said in a press release, “Historically, supersonic aircraft have been the work of nation states, developed by militaries and governments.” But the latest flight made the XB-1 “the world’s first independently developed supersonic jet ” to break the sound barrier, Boom Supersonic said.
sentences.zh: 该公司在一份新闻稿中说, “ 从历史上看,超音速飞机是国家由军队和政府开发的。 ”但最新的飞行使XB-1号“世界第一架独立开发的超音速喷气机”打破音障。

sentences.en: The company’s founder and chief executive officer, Blake Scholl, said, “XB-1’s supersonic flight demonstrates that the technology for passenger supersonic flight has arrived.”
sentences.zh: 该公司的创始人兼首席执行官Blake Scholl说,“XB-1的超音速飞行表明客机超音速飞行技术已经抵达。 ”

sentences.en: Boom Supersonic launched in 2014 “with the goal of making high-speed travel mainstream and enabling a new world of human connection.” With that in mind, the company has been working to develop a supersonic passenger airliner called Overture.
sentences.zh: 2014年启动的“超级超声波 ”, “ 目标是将高速旅行纳入主流,并促成一个新的人际联系世界 ” 。 考虑到这一点,该公司一直在开发一个名为“主动”的超声波客机。

sentences.en: The aircraft would carry up to 80 passengers.
sentences.zh: 该飞机将运载多达80名乘客。

sentences.en: Boom Supersonic is one of several American companies seeking to develop supersonic flight vehicles.
sentences.zh: 超级超音速号是几个美国公司之一 试图开发超音速飞行器

sentences.en: NASA is also working on a supersonic aircraft in partnership with a U.S. contractor.
sentences.zh: 美国航天局还与美国承包商合作研制了一架超音速飞机。

sentences.en: The last time supersonic travel was available to passengers was 2003.
sentences.zh: 上一次向乘客提供超音速旅行是2003年。

sentences.en: That is the year the Concorde – the world’s first supersonic passenger jet aircraft – stopped service.
sentences.zh: 这是康科德(Concorde ) — — 世界上首架超音速客机 — — 停止服务的一年。

sentences.en: Britain and France jointly operated the Concorde.
sentences.zh: 英国和法国共同管理协和。

sentences.en: But the joint operation between British Airways and Air France suffered several business difficulties that led to the decision to stop flying the supersonic planes.
sentences.zh: 但英国航空公司和法国航空公司之间的联合行动遇到了一些商业困难,导致决定停止飞超音速飞机。

sentences.en: Some of the difficulties were linked to publicity about a deadly Concorde crash in 2000.
sentences.zh: 其中一些困难与2000年一场致命的协和崩溃的公示有关。

sentences.en: That incident involved an Air France airliner crashing shortly after taking off from Paris.
sentences.zh: 这起事件涉及一架法国航空公司的客机在从巴黎起飞后不久坠毁。

sentences.en: The crash claimed a total of 113 lives. Boom Supersonic says its planned Overture airliner will be designed to transport passengers from the U.S.
sentences.zh: 坠机造成113人死亡。

sentences.en: East Coast across the Atlantic to Europe in about 3-and-a-half hours.
sentences.zh: 东海岸横跨大西洋到欧洲 大约3个半小时后

sentences.en: The flight with normal passenger jets takes about eight hours.
sentences.zh: 使用普通客机的飞行需要大约8个小时。

sentences.en: Amy Marino Spowart is the president and chief executive officer at the National Aeronautic Association.
sentences.zh: Amy Marino Spowart是国家航空协会的主席和首席执行官。

sentences.en: She told The Associated Press the latest supersonic test flight suggests “the future of aviation is here and now.” Spowart added, “Not only is there hope for faster and better commercial flight, but Boom proves that it can be done sustainably .”
sentences.zh: 她告诉美联社,最新的超声波测试飞行表明“航空的未来就在此时此地 ” 。 斯波瓦特补充说, “ 不仅有更快、更好的商业飞行的希望,而且砰也证明它可以持续进行。 ”

sentences.en: Boom Supersonic has said its planned supersonic airliner will be designed to run on up to 100 percent sustainable aircraft fuel.
sentences.zh: Boom Supersonic说,它计划中的超音速客机 将设计成可以100%持续运行的飞机燃料。

sentences.en: Such sustainable fuels are made from non-petroleum products, such as food waste or other biomass materials.
sentences.zh: 这种可持续燃料来自非石油产品,如食品废物或其他生物物质。

sentences.en: Both XB-1 and Overture are made mostly from a carbon-based composite material to provide “a strong, lightweight structure,” the company said.
sentences.zh: 该公司说,XB-1和Optition大部分是用基于碳的复合材料制作的,以提供“一个强大的轻量级结构”。

sentences.en: NASA’s supersonic aircraft – built together with Lockheed Martin – is called X-59.
sentences.zh: 美国航天局的超音速飞机 — — 与洛克希德·马丁一起建造 — — 被称为X-59。

sentences.en: It is also an experimental plane that is seeking to test the level of noise produced by supersonic travel.
sentences.zh: 这也是一架实验飞机,试图测试超音速旅行产生的噪音水平。

sentences.en: Currently, supersonic flights are banned over land because of the loud noise they produce.
sentences.zh: 目前,超音速飞行被禁止飞越陆地,因为它们产生的噪音很大。

sentences.en: NASA has explained it plans to carry out testing this year of the X-59 aircraft, which has been designed and engineered to operate at lower noise levels than other supersonic aircraft.
sentences.zh: 美国航天局解释说,它计划今年对X-59型飞机进行测试,该飞机的设计和设计是为了在比其他超音速飞机低的噪音水平上运行。

sentences.en: The tests – to take place at supersonic test centers in California – are designed “to prove the quiet supersonic technology works as designed.”
sentences.zh: 这些测试 — — 将在加利福尼亚州超音速测试中心进行 — — 旨在“证明超音速超音速技术在设计时有效 ” 。

sentences.en: NASA said that after that testing is done, the agency plans to begin community reaction studies, beginning in 2026.
sentences.zh: 美国航天局说,测试完成后,该机构计划从2026年开始开展社区反应研究。

sentences.en: These will involve flying the X-59 over several cities and then asking people on the ground to share their thoughts on the level of noise they heard.
sentences.zh: 这将涉及在几个城市上飞过X-59号,然后请地面上的人就他们听到的噪音程度交流他们的想法。

sentences.en: NASA has said the X-59 – which measures 30 meters long and nine meters wide – is expected to fly at 1.4 times the speed of sound.
sentences.zh: 美国航天局说,X-59号(测量30米长和9米宽)预计飞行速度为声音的1.4倍。

sentences.en: That is about 1,500 kilometers per hour.
sentences.zh: 大约每小时1500公里

sentences.en: I’m Bryan Lynn. The Associated Press, Reuters and Boom Supersonic reported on this story.
sentences.zh: 美联社、路透社、Bom Supersonic报导了这个故事。

sentences.en: Bryan Lynn adapted the reports for VOA Learning English.
sentences.zh: 布莱恩・林恩改编了报告 为VOA学习英语。

sentences.en: mainstream – adj. the beliefs or way of living that are accepted by most people enable – v. to make something possible sustainable – adj. method of energy production that cause little or no damage to the environment composite – adj. made up of several different materials or parts
sentences.zh: 主流-即大多数人所接受的信念或生活方式使得——相对于使某种东西成为可能的可持续-能源生产方法几乎或根本没有对环境综合体造成破坏-由若干不同材料或部分组成的adj.
